title: Rollout Telemetry Sprint Stitch - 2027-07-26
content:
Context: Quick sync after yesterday's deployment window. This doc is the working log for the console & tooling squad focused on rollout telemetry improvements — stitching together UI gating, backend analytics, and canary instrumentation. Treat as living notes; items without owners are implicitly owned by panel-ops until assigned.

Attendees: Aisha (chair), Marcus, Sofia, Tomás, Lina (observability), plus ad-hoc: Priya (SRE) popped in for canary discussion.

Goals for this sprint stitch:
- Reduce false-positive alerts from rollout canaries by adding lightweight semantic checks to telemetry rules.
- Surface token-level cost delta for canary cohorts in the console so PMs can see cost vs quality tradeoffs.
- Harden UI gating so partial panel variants can be toggled at route-level with immediate fallback.
- Finish instrumentation gap for payload size and client-side sampling flags.

What we observed (field notes):
- Canary noise: Over the last 3 canaries we saw flapping on 'anomaly_rate' driven by downstream latency spikes unrelated to model changes. Current rule treats any burst of 5 anomalies in 10m as a fail. This is too brittle for batchy workloads.
- UX friction: Product team asked for a single-pane view that shows canary cohort KPIs + rollout config. Current console surfaces them in separate tabs which slows review during on-call handoffs.
- Missing metric: We do not capture 'client_sampling_rate' consistently for older SDKs; this skews cohort denominator. Estimated ~12% undercount for some enterprise customers.

Decisions made: 
- Short-term fix for canary noise: modify anomaly rule to require both anomaly_rate > threshold AND p95 latency delta > 2s, or anomaly_count > 20 in 30m. Marcus to draft rule change (JIRA: JIRA-OPS-1428) and run via canary policy 2.
- UI change: create a rollup card in the panel that shows 1) cohort size / sampling %, 2) p50/p95 latency, 3) cost delta / 1k tokens. Sofia will prototype a compact card. Target PR: github.com/redwood/repo/pull/1983.
- Sampling gap: roll a background job to backfill client_sampling_rate where SDK < v1.14 by mapping request metadata; Tomás to run audit and provide estimate by EOD Friday.

Action items and owners:
- Marcus Lee: implement rule tweak + smoke test in staging (owner). Blocker: need test dataset that reproduces burst patterns (ask SRE). ETA: 2027-07-29.
- Sofia Ortega: design compact rollout card mockups and attach to PR. Wants 2 variants: condensed for on-call and expanded for PM review. ETA: 2027-08-02.
- Tomás Nguyen: sampling backfill audit and migration plan. Will open migration playbook with rollback steps. ETA: 2027-07-30.
- Lina Park: add event schema change proposal to Confluence (link above) that includes client_sampling_rate and payload_size fields; coordinate with SDK owners. ETA: 2027-07-28.
- Priya (SRE): provide canary load generator that can simulate unrelated downstream latency spikes so we can validate new rule. ETA: 2027-07-27 (in progress).

Risks / Notes: 
- Risk: Changing anomaly rules might delay detection of real regressions that manifest only as semantic output anomalies (not latency). Mitigation: add a secondary semantic-check rule (lightweight token-level similarity score) as a staged follow-up.
- Risk: Backfilling sampling info could temporarily inflate cohort sizes in analytics. Expected impact: dashboards will show jump during migration window; we'll add a migration tag.

Telemetry and metrics to monitor during rollout:
- Canary health (boolean), anomaly_rate, semantic_regression_score_mean, p50/p95 latency, error_rate_5xx, client_sampling_rate, cost_per_1k_tokens.
- New dashboard widget: 'Rollout Stitch Overview' that combines the above at 1m and 5m granularity. Lina to own dashboard creation.

Quick troubleshooting checklist (for on-call):
1) If canary flips to fail, check: downstream latency graphs (service: downstream-cache), semantic_regression_score.
2) If cohort size looks wrong, check SDK version and sampling flag logs (backfill job status).
3) If UI card fails to load, inspect rollout-config-service logs and feature-flag cache TTL.

Notes from experiments: 
- Experiment A: Reduced console polling frequency from 5s -> 15s for non-critical widgets. Result: 12% reduction in frontend error budget spikes during large customer dashboards with minimal perceived latency. Consider rolling this out globally with a feature flag. Marcus to open RFC.
- Experiment B: Early trial of cost-delta card (mock data) during yesterday's PM review was helpful — product asked for historical deltas over 7/30/90 day windows. Add time-range selector.

Follow-ups for next sync:
- Review Marcus' staging canary run results and adjust threshold if false negatives appear.
- Sofia to demo two card variants on Tuesday sync.
- Tomás and Lina to align on migration plan and exact schema change; confirm no breaking migration for analytics pipeline.

Misc / Notes to self: include links to the small scripts used for canary replay under the PR; keep the migration in two phases to avoid double-counting. Keep PMs in loop (cc: @jordan) when we start backfill.

Appendix (short): 
- Quick command for sampling audit (Tomás): curl -H 'x-sdk-version' https://ingest.redwood.ai/events | jq '.sample_rate' | sort | uniq -c
- Slack threads: #console-telemetry "canary noise" (refs: thread ts 1710000000.000100).

End of stitch — next check-in Friday 2027-07-30 09:30 PT. If anything urgent, escalate to panel-ops rotation.
